text:
maya: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-picker change I'm seeing slow steady GPU memory growth on the main serving pool. Not a hard OOM yet but up ~1.2GB after ~30m of mixed traffic.
cheng: ugh. Is this the same pattern as the KV cache snapshots we saw last quarter? or new?
maya: different. KV cache looks stable; growth shows up in allocator stats and per-GPU resident set. Pattern: small step increases on certain request shapes (long seq + sampling).
alex: can you paste the allocator summary and the nvtx snapshot?
maya: pasted below (snip). main-serving-gpu0 resident: 12.4GB -> 13.6GB over 1800 requests. allocator arena counts: arenas=4, large_free_frag=340MB, total_reserved=14.2GB, in_use=11.9GB. nvprof summary (truncated):
```
| timestamp | total_mem_allocated | active_blocks |
| t0       | 11.9GB              | 432           |
| t1000    | 12.4GB              | 439           |
| t1800    | 13.6GB              | 447           |
```
```
maya: full nsys trace uploaded: https://internal.corp/redwood/nsys/1799989999-sweep1
sam: thanks — first-pass: could be fragmentation from allocator splitting + small realloactions. Also possible KV-cache shadow allocations on sampling because of attention backwards?
cheng: can we reproduce in a short loop with a fixed prompt mix? If we can repro locally we can toggle allocator params.
maya: added repro script and run command:
```
# repro command
python devtools/repro_mem_growth.py --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 --sampling true
```
script prints per-iter resident and allocator_stats. early run shows +350MB / 50 iters.
alex: I'll try with arena_count=8 and workspace_reserve=512MB env flags. Please run both on CI GPU. Also try `REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1` which enables buffer reuse optimization.
ci-bot: triggered job: ci/repro/1799990000-repro-mem-growth (queued)
ops-bot: deployed test build with kernel-picker revert to canary-2 for canary pool at 1799990100
cheng: ran locally: with default allocator we saw growth; with `arena_count=8` growth rate reduced ~3x, with `REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1` growth nearly flat. Not definitive but suggests fragmentation and lack of reuse are big contributors.
maya: great. can you share the exact allocator stats for both runs?
cheng: default: free_frag=420MB, reserved=14.6GB, peak_inuse=12.1GB; arena8+reuse: free_frag=92MB, reserved=13.9GB, peak_inuse=12.0GB. Also noticed fewer small alloc ops in profiler (alloc_count per iter dropped from ~230 to ~88).
sam: that drop in small alloc ops is convincing for reuse helping. Still want to rule out a true leak. Can we run bisection on the kernel-picker PR? maybe it introduced a code path that creates ephemeral tensors without freeing order-safely.
maya: I'll start a git bisect between main@1799900000 and canary@1799970000 and wire the repro to return nonzero on growth > 400MB.

maya: bisect script snippet:
```
#!/bin/bash
# exit 1 if resident growth > threshold
python devtools/repro_mem_growth.py --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --iters 150 || exit 1
```
```

sam: also add a periodic `torch.cuda.memory_summary()` dump to the repro so we can see per-allocator buckets. Put output to /tmp/bisect-logs.
cheng: one more curious thing: the profiler snapshot shows a small number of orphaned device pointers in one callsite in runtime/kernel_dispatch.cpp line ~412. Could be racy free. I left an inline log there to print pointer ids.
alex: if it's racy we might only see it under certain seeding — add stress: `--parallel-requests 3` to repro to increase interleaving.
maya: CI job finished: ci/repro/1799990000-repro-mem-growth succeeded on canary with reuse flag but failed (growth > 400MB) on default. Logs: https://internal.corp/ci/1799990000/logs.
ci-bot: archived artifacts: /artifacts/1799990000/{nsys,allocator_stats,mem_summary.txt}
sam: next steps: 1) run bisect with reuse flag OFF to find offending commit, 2) add extra sanity free in kernel_dispatch around that callsite to test if double-free or missed free, 3) upstream a quick patch to enable reuse by default behind feature flag.
maya: agreed. I'm also capturing a full NVTX-flame timeline for a repro run with and without reuse to share with runtime team.
cheng: FYI I ran the bisect locally and narrowed to a change in kernel-picker where we allocate a transient per-request workspace object instead of reusing a thread-local workspace. That matches the allocator pattern.
alex: nice find. Proposal: rework kernel-picker to use pooled workspaces (TL pool) + enable REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE default for canary, monitor for 24h, then roll.
maya: I'll open a PR with pooled workspace + tests and include perf benchmarks. Tagging @eng-runtime for review.
sam: thumbs up. leave this thread open — if anyone sees an unexplained memory spike, drop logs here. :eyes:
maya: thanks everyone :heart:
